mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s bring together what Covert’s story really shows us. It’s the little, everyday moments of kindness that can quietly reshape a whole community. Real inclusion? It’s not just about what we say or believe—it’s about rolling up our sleeves and working together. And when we remember and share our history, it becomes a living act of hope and quiet resistance. Resilience isn’t just about standing tall in good times—it’s about leaning on each other when things get tough. And building connection? That’s a job that never ends. It’s something we have to choose, every single day. So, if you ever find yourself questioning whether real change is actually possible, Covert’s story gives us a gentle but clear answer: yes—but only if we’re ready to put in the effort. The people in this small town didn’t set out to make history. They simply kept choosing to see each other as neighbors, not strangers. Their courage wasn’t flashy. It was steady. Their hope wasn’t naive—it was earned, step by step. In a world that still wrestles with division and fear, their example gives us both comfort and a bit of a challenge. Here’s what this means for you. You don’t need to be a hero to make a difference. Start with a conversation, offer a helping hand, or just listen. Every act of inclusion, no matter how small, sends ripples far beyond what you can see. The legacy of Covert isn’t just a story from the past—it’s an open invitation to build real kinship, right where you are. This work keeps going, and you’re not doing it alone. So, take heart—and go ahead, take that next step.
